1. CALL TO ORDER AND ROLL CALL 
 
Mayor Lincoln called the East Palo Alto City Council Special Meeting to order at 6:03 PM. City 
Clerk James Colin confirmed a quorum was present.

2. APPROVAL OF THE AGENDA 
 
Motion: Mayor Lincoln moved, Councilmember Dinan seconded, to approve the agenda as 
proposed. Motion carried unanimously (5-0). 
 
3. APPROVAL OF THE CONSENT CALENDAR 
 
3.1 Residential Permit Parking Program Study Contract Award 
Recommendation: Adopt a resolution: 
1. Authorizing the City Manager to award, negotiate and execute an agreement with 
Dixon Resources Unlimited (DIXON), in a form approved by the City Attorney, in the 
 
amount of $232,850 with a 10% contingency in the amount of $23,285 for a not-to- 
exceed amount of $256,135 to conduct follow up studies and investigations 
 
associated with the Residential Permit Parking (RPP) Ordinance, for Option 1 
(DIXON-led data collection) of Task 2 together with Optional Services A, B, C and D 
as set forth in DIXON's cost proposal, the not-to-exceed amount being the maximum 
total payable to DIXON under the agreement, inclusive of all other direct costs, 
reimbursables, pass-through expenses and any time-and-materials billing; and 
2.Finding that the proposed action does not constitute a project with the meaning of the 
California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) pursuant to CEQA Guidelines sections 
15378(b)(4) and (5) in that it is a governmental fiscal, organizational or administrative 
3.2 FY 2025-26 Fourth Quarter Treasury Report 
Recommendation: 
Accept and file the Cash Treasury Report for the month of June 2026. 
3.3 FY 2025-2026 Capital Water System Improvement Payments to Veolia 
Recommendation: 
1. Authorizing the City Manager to reimburse Veolia for city-wide capital 
water system improvements and appropriating an amount not to 
exceed $296,110.00 from the Water Capital Fund for FY 25/26 for that 
purpose; and

2. Finding that the action being considered does not constitute a “Project” 
within the meaning of the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA), 
pursuant to CEQA Guideline section 15378 (b)(5), in that it is a 
government administrative activity that will not result in direct or indirect 
changes in the environment, and that pursuant to section 15301 (minor 
alterations) as it involves minor improvements to existing facilities.

3.9 Second Amendment Retroactively Extending the Term of the Agreement 
with Willdan Financial Services, and Ratification of Services Accepted 
and Payments Made After Expiration of the Term 
Recommendation: 
Adopt a resolution: 
 
1. Finding, on the basis of this report and the record, that the scope of 
services described below were previously authorized by the City, were 
actually and necessarily performed by Willdan Financial Services, 
conferred a direct benefit on the City and on the East Palo Alto Sanitary 
District, and that payment for those services serves a public purpose; 
 
2. Ratifying all acts of City officers and staff in requesting, accepting, and 
paying for services performed by Willdan Financial Services after 
expiration of the term of the Agreement on December 31, 2025, 
including the City Manager’s exercise of the six-month extension option.; 
 
3. Approving the City Manager to execute the Second Amendment; 
 
4. Ratifying payment of invoices totaling $12,000 paid to Willdan Financial 
Services after expiration of the term, and find that those payments are 
within the not-to-exceed amounts previously authorized by the City 
Council and were made from appropriations lawfully available at the 
time of payment; and 
 
5. Finding that the action is not a “project” within the meaning of the State 
CEQA Guidelines (Cal. Code Regs., tit. 14) section 15378(b)(5). [R2]

3.10 City Council Meeting Minutes 
Recommendation: Adopt the July 21, 2026, City Council Meeting Minutes 
 
113

Councilmember Romero and Councilmember Dinan pulled Items 3.3 and 3.4. 
 
Motion: Councilmember Romero moved; Councilmember Dinan seconded to approve the 
Consent Calendar, excluding Item 3.3 and 3.4. Motion carried unanimously. 
 
3.3 FY2025-2026 Capital Water System Improvement Payments to Veolia 
Councilmembers asked questions while Public Works Director Humza Javed confirmed 
information for the public. 
 
Motion: Councilmember Romero moved; Councilmember Dinan seconded to approve the 
payments to Veolia. Motion carried unanimously. 
 
3.4 Latino History Month Proclamation 
Vice Mayor Abrica offered remarks recognizing the City's 43rd Anniversary of Incorporation. 
 
Motion: Mayor Lincoln moved; Vice Mayor Abrica seconded to approve the proclamation. 
Motion carried unanimously. 
 
4. CLOSED SESSION 
 
No closed session was held. 
 
5. PUBLIC COMMENT 
 
The following speakers provided public comments: Gail Dixon, Bishop Dr. Cleveland Prince, 
Leland Francois, Mario Mendoa, Nevada Butler, and Lynelle Burleson. 
 
6. INFORMATIONAL REPORTS 
 
6.1 Climate Action Plan Implementation Report 
 
No action was taken; the report was received for information. 
 
7. SPECIAL PRESENTATIONS 
 
No special presentations were heard. 
 
8. PUBLIC HEARINGS 
 
8.1 Inclusionary Housing Alternative Compliance Option for 2120-2160 Euclid 
Ave Mixed-Use Project (Portion of APN 063-292-380) 
 
Staff presented the item, and public comment was received. Council approved that the proposed 
alternative compliance option for the 2120–2160 Euclid Avenue project meets IHO requirements, 
as amended to move 9 state density bonus units from 80% AMI to 50% AMI (resulting in 10 units 
at 50% AMI and 9 units at 80% AMI). 
 
Motion: Councilmember Romero moved, Vice Mayor Abrica seconded to adopt the resolution. 
Motion carried unanimously. 
8.2 Bell Street Park Easement for RCSD 2120 Euclid Avenue Project 
Staff and consultants presented the proposed options for Bell Street Park. Public comment was 
received. 
114

 
Motion: Councilmember Dinan moved, Councilmember Romero seconded to adopt the 
resolution granting the fire suppression access easement through Bell Street Park under Option 
3, with minor clerical corrections to the resolution to properly label the option. Motion carried 
unanimously. 
8.3 Annual Inclusionary Housing In-Lieu Fees Update 
This item was continued to a future meeting. No action was taken. 
 
9. POLICY AND ACTION 
 
No items were heard. 
10. ADJOURN CITY COUNCIL SPECIAL MEETING AND RECONVENE TO THE EAST 
PALO ALTO SANITARY DISTRICT 
11. EPASD CONSENT CALENDAR 
 
11.1 Cash Disbursement Report for June 2026 
 
Motion: Mayor Lincoln (Vice President) moved, and Vice Mayor Abrica (President) seconded to 
approve the EPASD Consent Calendar. Motion carried 5-0.

13. ADJOURN EAST PALO ALTO SANITARY DISTRICT MEETING AND RECONVENE

14. COUNCIL REPORTS 
 
Councilmember Romero: Requested transparency regarding records related to alleged ex parte 
communications with a developer. 
 
Mayor Lincoln: Requested future presentations on the Tonga delegation and emergency 
preparedness. 
 
Vice Mayor Abrica: Reported on recent community events and a County briefing on vehicle 
license fee impacts.
